title: 37.1 IBM Telum II Processor Design-Technology Co-Optimizations for Power, Performance, Area, and Reliability
problem: Designing a high-performance 5nm processor at scale requires simultaneous optimization of power, performance, area, and reliability while managing massive concurrent EDA and design complexity across libraries, IP blocks, and gate-level entities.
motivation: As transistor counts scale to 43B+ and wire complexity reaches 38km per die, monolithic design approaches break down; design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) becomes essential to extract value from advanced nodes.
method: IBM Telum II designs the processor and manufacturing process together, jointly optimizing both rather than designing first and fitting to the process later. The team created custom standard cells (basic circuit building blocks) and pre-made functional modules specifically tuned to a modified 5nm Samsung process. They designed different parts of the chip—memory arrays, storage registers, analog circuits, input/output interfaces, and custom logic—simultaneously instead of sequentially, surfacing conflicts early so everything can be optimized together. To handle the massive complexity of a 43-billion-transistor design, they built abstraction layers that organize design information at different levels of detail.
key_novelty: Concurrent hierarchical design lets teams simultaneously develop standard cell libraries (basic building blocks), IP blocks (pre-made functional modules), and gate-level logic (individual circuit elements), which manages the complexity of 43 billion transistors.
contributions: Design-technology co-optimization on modified 5nm Samsung bulk process
Custom standard cell and IP library enabling 1.3T shapes (1.25× density improvement)
Concurrent hierarchical design for 43B transistors across 18 BEOL layers
EDA innovations for abstraction and modeling at massive scale
